title: Count Paths That Can Form a Palindrome in a Tree
summary: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node i has a parent parent[i] and an edge character s[i], count the number of node pairs (u, v) where u < v and the edge characters on the path from u to v can be rearranged to form a palindrome.
statement: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node i has a parent parent[i] and an edge character s[i], count the number of node pairs (u, v) where u < v and the edge characters on the path from u to v can be rearranged to form a palindrome.
constraints: parent defines a rooted tree at node zero; character s[i] labels the edge from parent[i] to i for i>0.
Count unordered pairs of distinct nodes whose path characters can be rearranged into a palindrome.
A multiset forms a palindrome when at most one character count is odd.
hints: Represent odd character counts along each root path by a 26-bit XOR mask.
The mask on a path between two nodes is the XOR of their root masks.
For each node, count earlier masks equal to its mask or differing in one bit.
Those and only those XOR results have zero or one set bit, exactly the palindrome-rearrangement condition.
editorial: Those and only those XOR results have zero or one set bit, exactly the palindrome-rearrangement condition.

tests.explanation: The path parity masks produce eight node pairs with at most one odd character.
The sole path has one character and is palindromic.
